_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC section 4

deliverables.text: A logic reference sheet that writes the flood-damage clause as a symbolic conditional p -> q, with p and q labeled, and its converse, inverse, and true contrapositive, each in full English and in symbolic notation.
A single compound-statement truth table covering all four candidate rules from D1 side by side for the same p and q, with a written note identifying which columns are logically identical.
A negation table giving the correct logical negation of each of the four candidate rules' conclusions, with a written explanation of why negation is not the same operation as forming the inverse.
A classification memo translating at least four Appendix E appeal scenarios into symbolic conjunctions/disjunctions and evaluating each as true or false against D2's truth table.
A wrongly-denied-claims-caught count, per 100 appeals reviewed, for the Plain-Text Standard and the Mirror-Image Standard, computed from Appendix E's full constructed log using D1's rules.

appendices.title: California DOI 2025 Consumer Complaint Study: Homeowners Justified-Complaint Ratios

balance.argument_a: The Plain-Text Standard requires zero retraining cost, and on Appendix E's real 14-row constructed log it already catches 6 of 14 wrongly-denied rows -- 42.9 caught per 100 appeals reviewed, the same 6 rows the Mirror-Image Standard also catches. It misses only 1 of Appendix E's 14 rows relative to Option B (row 1), a real but narrow gap: Option B's 50.0-per-100 catch rate is only 16.7% higher, comfortably inside the 20% cap, for a standard that requires no new review step at all.
balance.argument_b: The Mirror-Image Standard catches 7 of Appendix E's 14 wrongly-denied rows -- 50.0 per 100 appeals reviewed, a real 16.7% higher catch rate than the Plain-Text Standard's 42.9 per 100 -- while denying coverage in the exact same true-flood cases (both standards agree on 13 of 14 rows, since a conditional and its contrapositive share every row of D2's truth table). The one additional catch (row 1) is a real converse-shaped misapplication only Option B's audit rule is structurally positioned to catch on appeal.
balance.margin_basis: Once Appendix E's full appeals log is populated (research or an accepted Modeling Assumption anchored to Appendix B's real justified-complaint-ratio range), classify every row under each candidate standard's own rule (D1), count wrongly-denied claims caught per 100 appeals under each (D5), and compute the percentage margin between the two rates the same way alert-curve's D5 computed its ratio margin.
balance.margin_note: Appendix E's 14-row constructed log (MA2) classifies as: 6 rows correctly denied (ground truth = flood, sound reasoning, both standards uphold, no catch needed) -- rows 2,4,6,8,10,12; 6 rows wrongly denied where a diligent reviewer applying either standard's own definition of 'flood' (Appendix A) would catch the misapplication on its face -- rows 3,5,7,9,11,13 (Plain-Text catches these too, since the adjuster's own stated reasoning contradicts the clause's definition without needing to check for a competing cause); 1 row (row 1, the case's own inciting windstorm scenario from the Overview) where the adjuster's stated reasoning merely labels the loss 'flood' without addressing the wind-created roof opening visible in the reported facts -- only the Mirror-Image Standard's explicit non-flood-cause check (per case.json balance.argument_b) catches this one, Plain-Text does not; and 1 row (row 14, the twist) where the competing cause was not visible in the file at review time at all, so neither standard catches it. Plain-Text Standard catches 6 of 14 wrongly-denied rows = 100*6/14 = 42.9 per 100 appeals reviewed. Mirror-Image Standard catches 7 of 14 (6 + the converse-shaped row) = 100*7/14 = 50.0 per 100 appeals reviewed. margin_pct = 100*(50.0-42.9)/42.9 = 16.7%, Mirror-Image Standard (Option B) winning -- inside the SPEC section 2 ~20% cap. Winning option: B.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA2: Appendix E's 14-row log is a constructed scenario dataset, not real appeal records (no insurer publishes its individual appeal files) -- the exact count of rows a diligent reviewer would catch under either standard is an author-chosen scenario mix, not a sourced figure. A -50% sweep (3 instead of 6 both-catch rows) pushes the margin to 33.3%, over the cap; the case's own real, published 14-row log (the row classification actually shipped) stays at 16.7%, and the case's own retune history (modeling_assumptions[MA2].sensitivity) already discloses this log was deliberately rebalanced once, from a 100%-margin draft, to land under the cap.

MA2: same basis as both_catch_rows -- the count of rows only the Mirror-Image Standard catches (row 1) is a constructed scenario choice, not sourced. A +50% sweep (1.5 instead of 1 row) pushes the margin to 25.0%, over the cap; the case's own shipped log (exactly 1 such row) stays at 16.7%.

Combine Anchors 2-3 into one pass. Run only one deep-conflict thread. Total runtime shortens proportionally; content does not.
No vote at Anchor 1 -- Marisol's opening position is stated instead of voted. The guide plays devil's advocate directly. The twist still lands; 'who reverses' becomes 'would you reverse, and why.'

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Adjusters on Marisol's appeals team have, in a real but unquantified share of cases, misapplied the flood-damage clause by reasoning from its converse rather than its true contrapositive.
modeling_assumptions.basis: No documented insurance-specific incident of this exact converse/contrapositive confusion was found in research. What is confirmed real: the underlying reasoning errors have standard, formally recognized names in formal logic -- 'affirming the consequent' (the converse error) and 'denying the antecedent' (the inverse error). CORRECTED 2026-09-01: a direct re-fetch of Carver v. Lehman, No. 06-35176 (9th Cir. 2008) found the opinion's own text does not discuss either fallacy by name (see S7's corrected note) -- the earlier claim that a real appellate opinion 'engages with the fallacy by name' was wrong and has been removed. This case states the specific insurance application as a scenario premise, openly -- not as a documented finding.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The case's entire premise for why the Mirror-Image Standard could outperform the Plain-Text Standard rests on this assumption being true to some meaningful degree in Appendix E's log; the case does not claim it is true of any real carrier.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Marisol's carrier (fictional): policy exposure count and 2024 justified-complaint ratio, Appendix B.
modeling_assumptions.basis: No real carrier's internal exposure count or complaint ratio for a fictional company can be sourced by definition. Exposure count (250,000) is chosen between the smallest (USAA General Indemnity, 159,197) and second-largest (Farmers Insurance Exchange, 439,921) of the four real named carriers in Appendix B, at the scale of a genuinely mid-size insurer. The 2024 ratio (18.5) is chosen inside the real observed 2024 range across those same four carriers (0.6 to 51.4, S1).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Low for the case's own math -- this row is scene-setting only; Appendix B's real four-carrier data (not this row) is what Background and Challenge D5 actually reference. Raising or lowering this figure does not change Appendix E's log or D5's count.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Appendix E's full 14-row constructed appeals log (all three columns, all 14 rows).
modeling_assumptions.basis: Constructed to give a realistic mix of correctly-denied flood claims (6 rows), plainly-misapplied non-flood claims a diligent reviewer under either standard should catch (6 rows), one converse-shaped misapplication a reviewer must actively check the reported facts to catch (1 row, the case's own inciting scenario from the Overview), and one file genuinely ambiguous at review time (1 row, the twist). No real institution's internal appeal log is used or implied. Its overall wrongly-denied share (8 of 14 rows) is anchored only qualitatively to Appendix B's real, dramatic 2024 shift -- the two figures use different units (per-100,000-exposures statewide vs. per-100-appeals in a small constructed log) and are never mathematically converted into one another.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: High -- this table is what Challenge D5's count and its percentage margin are computed from directly. A different constructed log could shift, or even reverse, which standard the count favors. RETUNED 2026-09-01: an earlier draft mix (3 both-catch rows, 3 Mirror-Image-only-catch rows) produced Plain-Text=3, Mirror-Image=6 per 14 rows, a 100% margin -- far outside SPEC section 2's ~20% cap. Retuned to 6 both-catch rows and 1 Mirror-Image-only-catch row (Plain-Text=6, Mirror-Image=7 per 14 rows), landing at 16.7%, safely under the cap, while preserving both failure modes (an obvious-misapplication row either standard catches, a converse-shaped row only the Mirror-Image Standard's checklist catches, and one row neither standard can catch because the competing cause is not visible in the file at review time).

sensitivity_note: Mildly sensitive per SPEC §6 and the concept sheet's own sensitivity flag: insurance claim denial touches a policyholder's home and money. Scenario is kept property/homeowners, not health or life, per the concept sheet's guidance. No illness, death, or acute family hardship is depicted -- comparable in register to this project's SOC/security-operations cases. Facilitator note in FACILITATOR.md.
